title: Binary Shock — PSR B1259−63 prototype
classification: Scientific visualization derived from an analytic axisymmetric model

decretion_disk.velocity_model: Keplerian rotation in the disk plane

shock_surface.color_field: Doppler factor toward the IBSEn line of sight

visual_interpretation.shock_alpha: Display mapping derived from normalized Doppler factor; not physical opacity
visual_interpretation.emission_and_halos: Artistic cues for visibility; browser glow is not baked into the GLB
visual_interpretation.pulsar_scale: Strongly enlarged; a physical neutron-star radius is unresolved at this scale
visual_interpretation.pressure_fields: Smooth browser volumes use the IBSEn pressure laws with contrast compression; both winds share one monotonic brightness mapping and spatial display window; brightness and opacity are display mappings, not gas density or physical opacity
visual_interpretation.disk_geometry: Diffuse browser volume sampled from the IBSEn radial pressure and vertical scale-height laws; no hard disk surface is stored in the GLB
visual_interpretation.disk_extent: IBSEn supplies no hard outer edge; the display radius is 1.35 times the pulsar's projected disk-plane radius and fades smoothly at the edge
visual_interpretation.turbulence: None added; the exported shock retains the axisymmetric IBSEn geometry
